producer_report.summary:
Study is now selectable, and Athena's own code pins firstmate's SHA when a study starts. The offline tests, clippy and fmt pass. I did not run the end-to-end job-start path with a study capability.

- **Config:** `athena.toml` has `[capabilities.study]` with producer and verifier commands, checks and env. Neither command list has `rm`, `mv`, `chmod`, `curl` or the network git verbs (`fetch`, `clone`, `pull`, `push`, `remote`, `ls-remote`); a test asserts this. `[capabilities.study.source]` holds firstmate's URL (from BRIEF.md) and `ref = "HEAD"`. No SHA is written anywhere. `config.rs` gains an optional `source` table (URL and ref) to parse it.
- **Hook:** the `Capability` trait gets `on_job_start`, which does nothing by default. `dispatch` in `run.rs` calls it before the producer brief is built. The brief gets a "Pinned source" note, and the hook's environment is merged into the agent and check env. A hook error stops the job before any dispatch commit.
- **Study:**
  - **Resolve:** the new `source.rs` runs `git ls-remote` through an injectable runner and accepts only a full 40-hex lowercase id. It refuses empty, short and non-hex results, remote failures, and URLs or refs that look like git options.
  - **Fetch:** it fetches exactly that commit, checks it out, deletes `.git`, and makes the tree read-only at `<job_dir>/source`.
  - **Expose:** the brief records the SHA, and the environment gets `ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_SHA`, `ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_DIR` and `ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_URL`.
- **Prompt:** one line replaced: "Source: pinned, read-only, present. Cite its recorded full SHA." The producer prompt budget test left no room for more.
- **Docs:** CHANGELOG, plus a new D75 in `docs/decisions.md` that cites the rejected earlier attempt. They say Athena resolves the SHA, the producer has no network, and no SHA is hand-recorded.
- **Tests:**
  - **Resolver:** a canned runner covers a ref resolving to a full SHA, refusal of bad results, and an unresolvable ref or failing remote. A local fixture repository covers a real pin.
  - **Hook:** the study start hook is tested directly with a fake runner; the same pin is exercised by `source.rs`'s local-fixture test. A `change` test shows the hook is a no-op.
  - **Wiring and grants:** a wiring test checks every registered capability has an `athena.toml` section, and the old "study is absent" assertion is replaced with grant checks.

Open: the tree sits outside the producer's snapshot, so it may not be readable under the path policy. See open_issues.

checks_run.note: Ran with --offline instead of --locked; Cargo.lock was updated by this change, and --locked fails only when the lock is stale.
Whole workspace passed, including the budgets test, the xtask policy and boundary-word tests, and the lifecycle tests.
Failed once, before Cargo.lock was regenerated. Rerun with --offline passed (35 tests).

open_issues: The pinned tree is at <job_dir>/source, outside the producer's snapshot directory. The producer's path policy may confine file reads to its snapshot, so the tree may not be readable by the producer. This needs checking, or the tree should be placed inside the snapshot, before a real study runs.

No test runs the full dispatch path with a study capability. The hook call in run.rs is exercised only by the existing lifecycle tests, which use the change capability. Study's hook is tested by calling it directly with an injected runner and a local fixture repository.
The ref is HEAD, so the pin follows firstmate's default branch at study start. The user may want a tag instead.
The producer's snapshot is created from the repository's base commit, so ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_DIR is only an absolute path. The driver's env filter may need to allow it through; I did not check that.
The checks in [capabilities.study] are fmt and test run on Athena's own repository; they are placeholders until the run step (D65) defines study-specific checks.
The pinned tree's directories are made read-only, so removing the job directory needs write permission restored first. Re-pinning does this itself; cleanup elsewhere does not.
mistakes: My first producer-prompt rewording pushed the producer token estimate over 1100 and failed the budgets test. I shortened it over four attempts until it passed.
learnings: The study producer prompt is held to a token budget by crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs: the producer set was within about 2 tokens of the 1100 cap, so any added prompt text needs equal removals.

docs/architecture.md lists each crate's allowed dependencies and a policy test checks them. I avoided a new athena-git dependency in athena-cap-study by running the git binary directly through std::process::Command.
Cargo.lock has to be regenerated (cargo ... --offline) after a Cargo.toml dependency change before --locked commands work.
CapabilityConfig has deny_unknown_fields, so new config keys need a struct field; I added an optional source table (url, ref).
BRIEF.md names firstmate's URL, https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate. I used it.
desires: A way to run the whole job-start path against a fake capability in the lifecycle tests, to prove end to end that dispatch calls the hook.
The firstmate URL and preferred ref from the user, instead of taking the URL from BRIEF.md.
